events.title: China Industrial Output Strengthens; Retail Sales Miss Forecast
events.description: China's industrial production growth accelerated in August on robust foreign demand, while retail sales logged a weaker growth and fixed asset investment downturn worsened further, underscoring the challenges in achieving the official growth target this year. events.title: Gold Drifts Lower On Firmer Dollar, Rising Oil And Bond Yields
events.description: Gold prices traded lower on Tuesday, extending losses from the previous session as investors weighed Middle East tensions and looked ahead to monetary policy meetings of central banks, including the U.S. Federal Reserve, the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan this week.

events.title: Oil Prices Rise On Middle East Supply Concerns
events.description: Oil prices rose sharply on Tuesday amid fears of a tightening oil market after Saudi Arabia closed a critical pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz following a drone attack.

events.title: European Shares Extend Losses As Banks Tumble On Oil-driven Inflation Fears
events.description: European stocks traded lower on Tuesday as surging oil prices and elevated bond yields weighed on the banking sector.

events.title: Asian Shares Retreat Ahead Of Fed Decision
events.description: Asian stocks ended mostly lower on Tuesday amid heightened Middle East tensions and concerns over the pace of artificial intelligence development.

events.title: UK Jobless Rate Remains Unchanged; Wage Growth Cools
events.description: The UK unemployment rate remained unchanged and wage growth eased in the three months to July period, reflecting the softening labor market conditions, data from the Office for National Statistics revealed Tuesday. The unemployment rate 4.9 percent in the three months to July, the same rate as in the quarter ended June. The rate was forecast to rise to 5.0 percent.

events.title: European Shares Set For Cautious Open
events.description: European stocks are seen opening on a cautious note on Tuesday as investors look ahead to monetary policy meetings of central banks, including the U.S. Federal Reserve, the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan this week.

events.title: Indian Shares Modestly Higher In Cautious Trade As IT Stocks Surge
events.description: Indian stocks were modestly higher in early trade on Tuesday, with information technology shares leading the surge, after industry leaders called for a slowdown in the pace of AI development.

events.title: Asian Markets Track Wall Street Lower
events.description: Asian stock markets are trading mostly lower on Tuesday, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight, as traders remain concerned about the uncertainty in the Middle East conflict. Higher bond yields and soaring crude oil prices fueled global inflation concerns and indicated an imminent interest rate hike from the US Fed this week. Asian markets closed mostly lower on Monday.

events.title: Indian Shares Seen Little Changed At Open
events.description: Indian shares are seen opening on a flat note on Tuesday as traders return to their desks after a long holiday weekend.

events.title: Lower Open Expected For Thai Stock Market
events.description: The Thai stock market has moved lower in four straight sessions, retreating almost 30 points or 1.9 percent along the way. The Stock Exchange of Thailand now sits just above the 1,590-point plateau and it's expected to spin its wheels again on Tuesday.

events.title: Indonesia Bourse May See Continued Consolidation On Tuesday
events.description: The Indonesia stock market has finished lower in four straight sessions, sinking more than 150 points or 2.3 percent along the way. The Jakarta Composite Index now sits just above the 6,530-point plateau and it's looking at another soft start again on Tuesday.

events.title: Japanese Market Modestly Lower
events.description: The Japanese stock market is trading modestly lower on Tuesday, extending the losses in the previous two sessions, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight, with the Nikkei 225 falling well below the 63,400 level, with weakness in automakers and financial stocks partially offset by gains in index heavyweights.
